disposition_reason: Original market survey: 72 consumer cocoa-containing products (e.g., dark chocolate) bought in the US in four cohorts (2014, 2016, 2019, 2022) analysed for Pb, Cd and total As by ICP-MS; Table 1 gives overall and per-cohort N/mean/median/min/max in µg/g. No per-product values are printed (Figures 1-3 are histograms of µg/serving).
disposition_locator: Methods p. 2; Table 1 p. 3; Figures 1-3 pp. 4-5

study.material_scope: consumer cocoa-containing products, 'such as dark chocolate'; product forms (bar vs powder vs other) not reported; Table 2 lists serving in 'g or mL'
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Purchase market: United States (online retailers, physical retailers, manufacturer websites), bought by ConsumerLab.com. 'All products were domestic or European produced'. Cocoa growing origin not reported.
study.collection_period: purchase cohorts 2014, 2016, 2019, 2022 (Table 3 labels the third cohort '2018')
study.sampling_unit: retail products (one result per product; products selected from yearly ConsumerLab popularity survey; higher-metal products often excluded from later cohorts)
study.method: Two US commercial laboratories; Pb: 0.5 g microwave digestion HNO3/HCl/H2O2 to 50 mL; As and Cd: 1 g hotplate HNO3 digestion to 200 mL; PerkinElmer NexION 350X ICP-MS; consistent with AOAC 2015.01; results above Prop 65 thresholds retested at one of two independent labs
study.lod_loq: Reporting limits: Pb 0.01 µg/g (10 µg/kg); As 0.02 µg/g (20 µg/kg); Cd 0.02 µg/g (20 µg/kg)
study.basis: product as sold (µg/g); per-serving and per-day doses derived from listed serving size assuming one serving/day
study.qa: Spike recovery QC limits 75-125%; calibration standards As 0.001-0.5 ppm, Pb/Cd 0.0005-0.02 ppm; second-source continuing check ±10% (0.1 ppm As, 0.01 ppm Pb/Cd). No CRM reported.

findings.material: consumer cocoa-containing products (e.g., dark chocolate); individual product forms not reported
findings.basis: product as sold (µg/g of product); no moisture or fat-free normalisation reported
findings.censoring: Reporting limits Pb 0.01 µg/g, As and Cd 0.02 µg/g (Methods). Source does not state how results below the reporting limit were entered; Table 1 prints values below these limits and a 0 minimum for Pb per serving. Not imputed here.

controls.control: Purchase non-organic rather than USDA-organic certified cocoa/dark chocolate products (organic label as a sourcing signal)
controls.comparator: organic vs non-organic products, controlling for number of certifications and cohort year (OLS, robust SE)
controls.outcome: Organic coefficient: Cd +0.401 µg/g (SE 0.148, p<0.01; +401 µg/kg); Pb +0.0202 µg/g (SE 0.00715, p<0.01; +20 µg/kg); tAs +0.0204 µg/g (SE 0.0141, n.s.). Panel FE per serving: Cd +3.163 µg/serving (p<0.05), Pb +0.0263 (n.s.), As +0.108 (p<0.1). Welch t-test Cd per day: not organic 3.176 µg/day (n=22, SD 3.914) vs organic 6.09 µg/day (n=15, SD 4.123), difference -2.91, t=-2.156, Pr(T<t)=0.0195; Pb and As not significantly higher in organic by Welch test.

controls.control: Number of third-party trade certifications (e.g., Fairtrade, Non-GMO) as a sourcing signal
controls.comparator: per additional certification, controlling for organic status and cohort year
controls.outcome: OLS µg/g: Pb -0.00896 per certification (SE 0.00300, p<0.01; -9 µg/kg), Cd -0.0745 (SE 0.0415, p<0.1), tAs -0.00432 (n.s.). Panel FE per serving: Pb +0.0195, Cd -0.674, As -0.0659 (all n.s.). Authors conclude certifications did not significantly alter metal levels.

controls.control: Cohort year (later product cohorts vs 2014) - market trend, not an intervention
controls.outcome: Pb µg/g contrasts vs 2014: 2016 -0.0391 (Bonferroni p=0.132), 2019 -0.0492 (p=0.020), 2022 -0.0466 (p=0.031). Cd: 2016 +0.0678 (p=1.0), 2019 -0.1975 (p=0.341), 2022 -0.3349 (p=0.009). As vs 2016: 2019 -0.1361 (p<0.0001), 2022 -0.1585 (p<0.0001). Caveat: higher-metal products were often excluded from later cohorts, so contrasts are not a causal or national trend.
controls.locator: Tables 3 and 5, PDF p. 6; Methods p. 2 (selection bias)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary describes the products as 'dark chocolate, cocoa powder, and related products' and sets matrices [dark-chocolate, cocoa-powder]; the primary text never says cocoa powder was tested - it says 'cocoa-containing products' 'such as dark chocolate', and Table 2 gives serving in 'g or mL', implying some liquid/other products.
Stored summary gives per-serving Cd mean 6.986 without noting that the Results text reports 4.358 µg/serving (which Table 1 prints as the per-day value, n=37).
Stored summary lists Table 1 cohort data but does not flag that minima (Pb 0.009, Cd 0.016, As 0.017 µg/g) are below the stated reporting limits, nor the As 2016 median = max = 0.2 artefact.
Stored summary 'Cohort interpretation' correctly notes the 2018/2019 label conflict (Table 3 vs Methods/Table 1); retained here.
unresolved: No per-product (sample-level) values are printed; Figures 1-3 are histograms of µg/serving by cohort only. Data availability statement says raw data available from authors on request - not obtained (no downloads permitted).

Product forms (dark chocolate bars vs cocoa powder vs beverages or other cocoa-containing foods) are not disclosed, so in-scope vs out-of-scope (e.g., drinks, confectionery) cannot be separated; all findings carry form 'mixed_products'.
Third cohort year is '2019' in Methods/Table 1/Table 5 but '2018' in Table 3; years recorded as 2019 per Table 1.
How sub-reporting-limit results were entered (reported value, RL, zero) is not stated; minima below RL and a zero Pb per-serving minimum suggest inconsistent conventions.
Table 4 'Combined' Std. dev. printed as 31.5013 is inconsistent with group SDs ~3.9-4.1 (likely typo for ~4.2); not used.
Cohort composition: higher-metal products were often excluded from subsequent cohorts, so cohort statistics are not comparable population estimates.
notes: Arsenic is total arsenic (tAs); no speciation. All concentration values are as-sold product µg/g converted ×1000 to µg/kg. Per-serving/per-day rows are retained as dose findings with value_ug_kg null.
